title: AATIP study of 260,000 cases and a possible existential threat

tellings.quote: And the the AATIP program looked at 260,000 different cases with seven levels of analysis. This is probably the biggest study of UFO data ever. And one of the conclusions that Vallée hints at two or three times in the journals is that you know, an existential threat may have been detected.

plain: AATIP was a small Pentagon office, run with the private company Bigelow Aerospace between about 2007 and 2013, that studied unexplained aerial reports. According to the researcher Jason Simosa, it went through 260,000 cases using seven levels of analysis, which he calls probably the biggest study of UFO data ever done. Simosa says that the computer scientist and longtime UFO researcher Jacques Vallée hints two or three times in his published journals at one of its conclusions: that "an existential threat may have been detected," which would mean the study found something it saw as a danger to humanity.
